payloads: ROLSES (Radio Observations of the Lunar Surface)
SCALPSS (Stereo Cameras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies)
description: First commercial soft landing on the Moon under NASA's CLPS initiative, delivering six NASA science and technology payloads to the rugged South Pole highlands near Malapert A.

ephemeris.sunElevation: 8.4° above local horizon (Low-angle polar grazing illumination)
ephemeris.earthElevation: 9.8° above local horizon (Direct-to-Earth line of sight)
ephemeris.powerAssessment: ~144 hrs continuous solar illumination before polar night
ephemeris.commAssessment: Direct S-band / X-band link to Earth; minor crater rim masking

terrain.topography: Highland crater rim terrain, ~12° local slope (LRO LOLA data)
terrain.horizonMask: Malapert massif elevates local northern horizon by ~6.5°
terrain.partnerContext: Supports Artemis South Pole navigation & plume-regolith baseline studies

payloads: LISTER (Lunar Instrumentation for Subsurface Thermal Exploration)
description: Delivered 10 NASA science and technology instruments to Mare Crisium to investigate subsurface heat flow, plume-surface interactions, and Earth's magnetosphere in X-rays.

ephemeris.sunElevation: 42.0° mid-day peak (Full 14-day lunar day illumination cycle)
ephemeris.powerAssessment: Optimal solar array output across 340+ hours of sunlit operations
ephemeris.commAssessment: Unobstructed Direct-to-Earth high-rate telemetry across Mare basin

terrain.topography: Smooth basaltic mare plain near Mons Latreille, <3° average slope
terrain.horizonMask: Low <1.5° horizon obstruction; ideal 360° field of view for LEXI imager
terrain.partnerContext: Calibrates lunar interior thermal models & international laser ranging networks

payloads: TRIDENT (The Regolith and Ice Drill for Exploring New Terrain)
description: Polar Resources Ice Mining Experiment-1 targeting the flat-topped Mons Mouton plateau near the Lunar South Pole to drill and analyze subsurface regolith for water ice.

ephemeris.sunElevation: 4.9° grazing polar sun angle (Long shadow regime)
ephemeris.powerAssessment: Vertical solar panels required to capture low-elevation polar sunlight
ephemeris.commAssessment: Direct-to-Earth window sensitive to local ridge elevation along azimuth 0°

terrain.topography: Elevated polar plateau (~6,000 m altitude), adjacent to cold-trap craters
terrain.horizonMask: Plateau elevation minimizes horizon blockage compared to surrounding basins
terrain.partnerContext: In-situ resource utilization (ISRU) precursor for Artemis & CSA lunar surface ops

description: Heavy-class commercial lunar lander mission targeting the illuminated rim of Nobile Crater at the Lunar South Pole to demonstrate precision hazard avoidance and rover deployment.

ephemeris.sunElevation: 3.8° above local horizon (Extreme South Pole illumination constraints)
ephemeris.earthElevation: 4.7° above local horizon (Requires high-gain directional antenna)
ephemeris.powerAssessment: Targeted landing during peak polar summer illumination period
ephemeris.commAssessment: Direct-to-Earth link supplemented by orbital relay pass windows

terrain.topography: Heavily cratered polar highland ridge bordering permanently shadowed regions
terrain.horizonMask: Complex local horizon (2°–9° masks) analyzed via LRO Quickmap DEMs
terrain.partnerContext: Includes commercial & Canadian Space Agency (CSA) micro-rover technology heritage

payloads: LITMS (Lunar Interior Temperature and Materials Suite)
description: CLPS delivery to the far side of the Moon inside the 320-km wide Schrödinger impact basin to study lunar seismicity, internal heat flow, and electromagnetic properties.

ephemeris.earthElevation: -38.2° (Below horizon — Earth is never visible from lunar far side)
ephemeris.powerAssessment: Solar arrays + high-capacity thermal/battery survival for lunar night
ephemeris.commAssessment: Zero Direct-to-Earth visibility; 100% reliant on lunar relay orbiter

terrain.topography: Inner peak-ring floor of Schrödinger impact basin, low boulder density
terrain.horizonMask: Basin walls & peak ring visible at 3°–5° elevation on Moon Trek 3D view
terrain.partnerContext: Advances international lunar geophysical network goals shared by NASA & CSA

description: Two-stage mission deploying an orbital communications relay satellite and landing the LuSEE-Night radio telescope on the radio-quiet far side of the Moon.

ephemeris.sunElevation: 44.5° maximum solar elevation at mid-southern latitude
ephemeris.earthElevation: -54.0° (Earth permanently shielded by lunar bulk for radio silence)
ephemeris.powerAssessment: Full 14-day solar charging + heavy battery pack for night radio observations
ephemeris.commAssessment: Relayed via Elytra Dark & Lunar Pathfinder satellites in elliptical lunar orbit

terrain.topography: Highland plains selected via LRO Quickmap for flat antenna deployment
terrain.horizonMask: Shielded from terrestrial radio frequency interference (RFI)
terrain.partnerContext: Demonstrates international relay architecture for far-side & polar exploration
